children: OAKVILLE, ON, Nov. 26, 2026 /CNW/ -- SIR Royalty Income Fund (TSX: SRV.UN) (the "Fund") today announced that SIR Corp. ("SIR" or the "Company"), the operating entity from which the Fund's equity income is ultimately derived, has filed its financial results for the 16-week and 52-week periods ended August 30, 2026 ("Q4 2026" and "Fiscal 2026", respectively). SIR's audited consolidated financial statements and management's discussion & analysis ("MD&A") for Fiscal 2026 can be accessed via the Fund's profile on the SEDAR+ website at
under "Other", or the SIR website at

SIR's Fiscal 2026 year consisted of 52 weeks compared to 53 weeks for Fiscal 2025, and the Company's Q4 2026 consisted of 16 weeks compared to 17 weeks for the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2025. Therefore, all financial information provided in this news release for the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2025 and for Fiscal 2025, unless otherwise noted, includes an additional week of operations that should be considered when comparing to the current year periods.
Food and beverage revenue from corporate restaurant operations increased by 3.3% to $103.7 million, compared to $100.4 million for the 17-week period ended August 31, 2025 ("Q4 2025").
Consolidated Same Store Sales ("SSS") (1) decreased by 1.6%. If the additional week of revenue, as described above, was removed from Q4 2025, consolidated SSS(1) for Q4 2026 increased by 4.9%.

On July 29, 2026, SIR opened a new Scaddabush Italian Kitchen & Bar® ("Scaddabush") location in Aurora, Ontario. This new restaurant is expected to be added to the Royalty Pooled Restaurants (the "Royalty Pool") effective January 1, 2027.
On September 23, 2026, SIR opened a new Scaddabush location in Kanata, Ontario. This new restaurant is expected to be added to the Royalty Pooled Restaurants effective January 1, 2027.

SIR has advised the Fund that food and beverage revenue from corporate restaurant operations totaled $103.7 million and $306.3 million in Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026, respectively, representing increases of 3.3% and 5.8% compared to $100.4 million and $289.4 million in Q4 2025 and Fiscal 2025 (the 53-week period ended August 31, 2025), respectively. The increases were primarily attributable to the opening of new Scaddabush locations in Barrie, Ontario (during Q4 2025), Windsor, Ontario (during Q3 2026) and Aurora, Ontario (during Q4 2026), as well as a new Jack Astor's® Bar and Grill ("Jack Astor's") + Freida's Beverage Kitchen ("Freida's") location in Oshawa, Ontario (during Q2 2025). These factors were partially offset by the permanent closures of the Jack Astor's location in Longueuil, Quebec (during Q3 2025) and the Duke's Refresher® + Bar ("Duke's Refresher") location at Queen Street East and Broadview Avenue in Toronto (during Q1 2026), as well as the temporary closures of the Jack Astor's locations in Barrie, Ontario (during Q1 2026) and Richmond Hill, Ontario (during Q3 2026) to complete renovations. The year-over-year increase in Q4 2026 was also partially offset by a 1.6% decline in consolidated SSS(1) for the quarter. The year-over-year increase for Fiscal 2026 also reflected consolidated SSS(1) growth of 1.8% for the year.

SSS(1) performance includes all SIR restaurants, except for those restaurants that were not open for the entire comparable periods in Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025. Accordingly, SSS(1) performance for Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026 does not include the new Jack Astor's restaurant in Oshawa, Ontario, and the new Scaddabush restaurants in Aurora, Barrie, Kanata and Windsor, Ontario. The closed Jack Astor's locations in North York, Ontario and Longueuil, Quebec, and the closed Duke's Refresher at the intersection of Queen Street East and Broadview Avenue in Toronto are also not included. The seasonal Abbey's Bakehouse® is also not included as it is not a SIR restaurant.

If the additional week of revenue was removed from revenue in Fiscal 2025, SSS(1) growth for each of the Concept and Signature Restaurants would be as follows, for Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026, respectively: Jack Astor's 4.4% and 2.9%, Scaddabush 3.4% and 4.5%, and the Signature Restaurants 14.8% and 10.6%. Consolidated SSS(1) increases for Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026 would be 4.9% and 4.0%, respectively.

Net loss and comprehensive loss was $0.1 million for Q4 2026, compared to net loss and comprehensive loss of $19.3 million for Q4 2025. Net loss and comprehensive loss was $15.3 million for Fiscal 2026, compared to $26.6 million for Fiscal 2025. The positive variances in Q4 2026 compared to Q4 2025 and Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025 primarily reflected the change in the amortized cost of the Ordinary LP Units and Class A Units of the SIR Royalty Limited Partnership (the "Partnership") that SIR holds, lower interest costs and increased earnings from restaurant operations, partially offset by increased cost of corporate restaurant operations.

For Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026, the change in amortized cost the Ordinary LP Units and Class A Units of the Partnership resulted in expenses of $7.3 million and $25.2 million, respectively, reflecting an increase in the underlying Fund unit price compared to the end of Q3 2026 and Fiscal 2025, respectively. For Q4 2025 and Fiscal 2025, the change in amortized cost resulted in expenses of $26.4 million and $36.4 million, respectively, reflecting increases in the underlying Fund unit price compared to the end of Q3 2025 and Fiscal 2024, respectively.

Adjusted Net Earnings(2) were $7.1 million in Q4 2026, compared to $7.2 million in Q4 2025. The slight decrease was primarily attributable to an increase in cost of corporate restaurant operations, partially offset by an increase in revenue from corporate restaurant operations and decreases in corporate costs and interest expense. Adjusted Net Earnings(2) were $9.9 million in Fiscal 2026, compared to $9.8 million in Fiscal 2025. The increase is primarily attributable to an increase in revenue from corporate restaurant operations and a decrease in interest expense, partially offset by increases in cost of corporate restaurant operations, corporate costs and other expenses.

As at August 30, 2026, SIR had cash (net of the cash balance of the Partnership) of $8.4 million compared to $12.5 million as at August 31, 2025, and had drawn approximately $37.7 million against the $68.0 million maximum principal borrowing amount under the Company's credit facilities.

SIR continues to monitor consumer spending behavior in light of current evolving macroeconomic factors, including inflation, interest rates and the impact of cross-border tariffs between Canada and the United States, and their potential impact on the Canadian economy and consumer confidence. Ongoing business impacts due to changes in the minimum wage and rising commodity costs have been influential in the bar and restaurant industry's changes in pricing overall.

SIR continues to innovate and provide immersive new product and service offerings to increase dine-in guest visits and to capitalize on the growth of take-out and delivery services in commercial foodservice.

The Jack Astor's + Freida's location in Oshawa, Ontario, and three new Scaddabush locations in Aurora, Windsor and Kanata, Ontario are expected to be added to the Royalty Pooled Restaurants effective January 1, 2027.

SIR has leased two properties – in London, Ontario and Dartmouth, Nova Scotia – upon which it plans to develop two new Scaddabush locations. SIR has also leased a property in Windsor, Ontario upon which it plans to develop a new Jack Astor's + Freida's location. There can be no assurance at this time that these planned new restaurants will be opened, or that any of these five new locations will become part of the Royalty Pooled Restaurants.

SIR is pursuing additional sites to continue the successful growth of its Scaddabush and Jack Astor's + Freida's concepts. SIR will also continue its practice of investing in existing restaurants to drive improved sales and earnings. In consideration of the ongoing economic and market conditions mentioned above, restaurant opening and renovation plans will be reviewed regularly and adjusted as necessary.

SIR Corp. is a privately held Canadian corporation that owns a portfolio of 57 restaurants in Canada. SIR's Concept brands include Jack Astor's Bar and Grill®, including Jack Astor's + Freida's Beverage Kitchen™, with 36 locations, and Scaddabush Italian Kitchen & Bar® with 17 locations. SIR also operates one-of-a-kind "Signature" brands including The Loose Moose®, REDS® Square One and Edna + Vita®. All trademarks related to the Concept and Signature brands noted above are used by SIR under a License and Royalty Agreement with SIR Royalty Limited Partnership. SIR also owns a Duke's Refresher® + Bar location, which is currently not part of the Royalty Pool. For more information on SIR or the SIR Royalty Income Fund, please visit

The Fund is a trust governed by the laws of the province of Ontario that receives distribution income from its investment in the SIR Royalty Limited Partnership and interest income from the SIR Loan. The Fund intends to pay distributions to unitholders on a monthly basis.

(1) Same store sales ("SSS") and same store sales growth ("SSSG") are non-GAAP financial measures and do not have standardized meanings prescribed by International Financial Reporting Standards ("IFRS"). However, SIR believes that SSS and SSSG are useful measures and provide investors with an indication of the change in year-over-year sales. SIR's method of calculating SSS and SSSG may differ from those of other issuers and accordingly, SSS and SSSG may not be comparable to measures used by other issuers. SSSG is the percentage increase in SSS over the prior comparable period. SSS includes revenue from all SIR restaurants except for those restaurants that were not open for the entire comparable period and Abbey's Bakehouse in Muskoka, Ontario as it is not a SIR restaurant. When a SIR Restaurant is closed, the revenue for the closed restaurant is excluded from the calculation of SSS for both the quarter in which the restaurant is closed and the current year-to-date.
(2) Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) is calculated by removing the change in amortized cost of the Ordinary LP Units and Class A LP Units of the Partnership from the net income (loss)

and comprehensive income (loss) for the period. Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) is a non-GAAP financial measure and does not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS. Management believes that in addition to net income (loss)

and comprehensive income (loss), Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) is a useful supplemental measure to evaluate SIR's performance. Changes in the amortized cost of the Ordinary LP Units and Class A LP Units of the Partnership is a non-cash transaction and varies with changes in the market price of the Fund units. The exclusion of the change in amortized cost of the Ordinary LP Units and Class A LP Units of the Partnership eliminates this non-cash impact. Management cautions investors that Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) should not replace net income (loss)

and comprehensive income (loss) or cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities (as determined in accordance with IFRS), as an indicator of SIR's performance. SIR's method of calculating Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) may differ from the methods used by other issuers. Please refer to the reconciliation of net income
and comprehensive income (loss) to Adjusted Net Earnings (Loss) for Q4 2026 and Fiscal 2026 provided in this news release.
